scope: Proposition 2.2 (Hartogs metric transfer) of the manuscript “A negatively pinched Kähler threefold without bounded holomorphic coordinates” (preprints/A-negatively-pinched-Kahler-threefold-without-bounded-holomorphic-coordinates-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 359 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 59e7bcf19b96d5d9), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 5. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let ϕ ∈ C∞(B, R) satisfy (2.2) and (2.3) for fixed 0 < c ≤ C < ∞. There is a finite λ0 = λ0(c, C) > 0 such that, for every λ ≥ λ0, the domain Mϕ in (2.5) is contractible and the tensor gλ = 2 Re b gλ defined by (2.6) is a smooth geodesically complete Kähler metric. For this fixed λ there are constants 0 < Aλ ≤ Bλ < ∞ such that −Bλ ≤ Kgλ (σ) ≤ −Aλ < 0 for every point of Mϕ and every real two-plane σ in its tangent space.
